_: What a configuration is: <nodes>/<class>/<method>/<attach>, e.g. 8/net/mesh/direct. tools/configuration.py is the only thing that parses one; everything else asks it. The design is docs/attachment-methods.md. A value with implemented=false is a real method or attachment MXFS does not have yet; it is named here so the grammar has a place for it, and a configuration using it is refused until it exists. The native-XFS baseline is not a configuration of MXFS and is spelled 1/xfs.

net.doc: lock state is held in node memory and exchanged over the interconnect

disk.doc: lock state lives on the shared LUN and is claimed with a storage primitive

net/mesh.doc: peer-to-peer network DLM; lock mastership is spread across the members

net/server.doc: a central lock server (or active/standby pair) holds every lock

disk/caw.doc: SCSI COMPARE AND WRITE on a lock block

disk/reserve.doc: SCSI-2 RESERVE/RELEASE around a plain lock-block write

disk/pr.doc: SCSI persistent reservations as the lock, or guarding its write

disk/fused.doc: NVMe fused Compare+Write; the Linux block layer cannot issue it today

disk/paxos.doc: Disk Paxos / Disk Lease: consensus on plain reads and writes

direct.doc: each node's own initiator, one path: an in-guest iSCSI login to the rig's SCST target on one portal

mpath.doc: each node's own initiator over two or more paths, assembled by dm-multipath

pass.doc: the hypervisor's initiator; the disk is passed into the VM as a SCSI LUN

drbd.doc: DRBD dual-primary replica of two local disks, admitted by its witness and fenced by its own proof profile instead of SCSI reservations (docs/attachment-methods.md). Released in 0.90.41 as 2/net/mesh/drbd, withdrawn on 2026-10-06 after it failed under eight concurrent VM installs on two physical Proxmox VE 9 hosts, released again in 0.90.107. The 'own_rig' flag says the attachment is verified by its own rig and board (scripts/drbd_rig.sh, MXFS_OWN_RIG=1) and is not a column of data/criteria.json or an entry of release_matrix; it says nothing about release status

shared.doc: a disk two VMs share through the hypervisor with no reservation fence MeshXFS can use (a vSphere multi-writer VMDK, which forwards no SCSI arbitration, or a physical-mode RDM, whose reservation key ESXi drops when it powers the VM off): two nodes, the network lock manager, compare-and-swap emulated on the disk, and a node fenced by its boot ending (fence=vcenter or fence=manual) instead of by the storage (docs/shared-disk-attachment.md). The devices are the lab VMDK and the cross-host RDM on vstest1/vstest2. The 'own_rig' flag says it is verified by its own harness (tests/vsphere_shared_fence.sh, MXFS_OWN_RIG=1) and is not a column of data/criteria.json or an entry of release_matrix

baseline.doc: native XFS on one node, no mxfs.ko: what the 2x performance ceiling is measured against

released_earlier._: Configurations an earlier release claimed that the current one does not: each was verified on the version named, and open records in the defect queue that cross the release bar reach it now (tools/defects.py <configuration> --release), so it is not re-verified or claimed until they are fixed. tools/release_text_check.py requires the README to list exactly these, with that version. 8/16 net/mesh/direct and 2-16 net/mesh/mpath were here from 0.90.51 until 0.90.130 verified them again. 2/net/mesh/direct and 2/net/mesh/mpath are claimed again by 0.90.131 (the packaged default is the network lock manager, and every platform row is graded on 2/net/mesh/direct); a net/mesh configuration still listed here is one an open record that crosses the release bar reaches.

released_by_own_rig._: Configurations a release claims that are verified by a rig and board of their own instead of a column of data/criteria.json. tools/release_text_check.py counts them as released when it checks the public text; scripts/release.sh --publish requires the named evidence for the version being published. 2/net/mesh/drbd was here from 0.90.41 (verified by tests/drbd_release_verify.sh, Ubuntu 24.04, DRBD 8.4.11), was withdrawn on 2026-10-06 when it failed under eight concurrent VM installs on two physical Proxmox VE 9 hosts, and has been here again from 0.90.107.

retired_keys._: The condition codes the rig used before 0.90.37. A tool given one refuses it and names the replacement; only the migrations translate them.
